rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: **Naked seeds.** Gymnosperms bear seeds that are not enclosed in a fruit; ovules lie exposed on the surface of megasporophylls, usually in cones.  ·  **Plant body.** They are mostly evergreen, woody trees and shrubs with well-developed roots (often with mycorrhizae) and needle-like or scale-like leaves.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: **Reproduction.** Male cones release pollen carried by wind to female cones; the ovule contains the female gametophyte and fertilisation gives a seed with a stored food supply.  ·  **Examples.** Cycas, Pinus, Cedrus (deodar), Ginkgo and Ephedra are familiar gymnosperms; Cycas retains fern-like leaflets and coralloid roots with nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria.  ·  **Economic importance.** Gymnosperms give timber, resins, turpentine, ephedrine (medicine) and ornamentals; their pollen can also cause allergies.
